title: Use an On/Off switch for Keyboard brightness control when there are only two states
line: Keyboard backlights that can only be on or off now get an on/off switch in Brightness & Color instead of a one-step slider.
explanation: The Brightness & Color popup always used BrightnessItem's slider for the keyboard backlight, even when the backlight only has two levels (UPower max brightness 1), so turning it on or off meant dragging a slider with a single step. BrightnessItem now shows a switch instead of the slider when its range is only 0 to 1; clicking it (or pressing Space when the row has keyboard focus) sets the brightness to 0 or 1, and it follows outside changes. The header keeps its Off/On label, and backlights with more levels keep the slider.

commits.message:
applets/brightness: use a switch for backlights with only two states

Keyboard backlights that can only be turned on or off were shown with a
slider that has a single step, which is an awkward way to flip a toggle.
When the item only has the off and on states, show a switch instead.

BUG: 489416

patches.diff:
From c428ea9855a2c53336daf8e8d2ca88171ba71b21 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 19:58:06 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] applets/brightness: use a switch for backlights with only two
 states

Keyboard backlights that can only be turned on or off were shown with a
slider that has a single step, which is an awkward way to flip a toggle.
When the item only has the off and on states, show a switch instead.

BUG: 489416
---
 applets/brightness/BrightnessItem.qml | 19 +++++++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 19 insertions(+)

diff --git a/applets/brightness/BrightnessItem.qml b/applets/brightness/BrightnessItem.qml
index 0963b509f..184e2eff7 100644
--- a/applets/brightness/BrightnessItem.qml
+++ b/applets/brightness/BrightnessItem.qml
@@ -55,7 +55,9 @@ PlasmaComponents3.ItemDelegate {
 
     Accessible.name: root.text
     Accessible.description: root.labelText
+    Accessible.onPressAction: if (toggle.visible) toggle.click()
     Keys.forwardTo: [slider]
+    Keys.onSpacePressed: if (toggle.visible) toggle.click()
 
     contentItem: RowLayout {
         spacing: Kirigami.Units.gridUnit
@@ -117,6 +119,7 @@ PlasmaComponents3.ItemDelegate {
             PlasmaComponents3.Slider {
                 id: control
                 Layout.fillWidth: true
+                visible: !toggle.visible
 
                 activeFocusOnTab: false
                 from: 0
@@ -136,6 +139,22 @@ PlasmaComponents3.ItemDelegate {
                     root.moved(value)
                 }
             }
+
+            PlasmaComponents3.Switch {
+                id: toggle
+                Layout.topMargin: Kirigami.Units.smallSpacing
+                visible: root.minimumValue == 0 && root.maximumValue == 1
+
+                activeFocusOnTab: false
+                focusPolicy: Qt.NoFocus
+                checked: root.value > 0
+
+                Accessible.name: root.text
+                Accessible.description: brightnessValue.text
+                Accessible.ignored: true
+
+                onClicked: root.moved(checked ? 1 : 0)
+            }
         }
     }
 }
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Master: a two-state keyboard backlight gets a slider with a single step, labelled On
With the fix: the same backlight gets an on/off switch, like Night Light and Dark Mode below it

reviews.text: The visual layout and UX of replacing the two-state keyboard backlight slider with a Switch in BrightnessItem.qml are clean and match the rest of the Brightness & Color popup. However, using onClicked on PlasmaComponents3.Switch breaks dragging the switch handle (which emits toggled rather than clicked, leaving the switch out of sync with the backlight), Keys.forwardTo still routes keys to the hidden slider, and accessibility properties on the switch are dead while the delegate itself does not expose checkable/checked state.
changes: Use onToggled instead of onClicked on the PlasmaComponents3.Switch so dragging the switch handle also triggers root.moved(checked ? 1 : 0); update Keys.onSpacePressed and Accessible.onPressAction accordingly (e.g. calling root.moved(root.value > 0 ? 0 : 1) or forwarding keys to toggle, since AbstractButton::click() does not emit toggled()).
Stop forwarding keys to the hidden Slider when the switch is shown (e.g. Keys.forwardTo: toggle.visible ? [toggle] : [slider] or toggle.visible ? [] : [slider]).

Clean up accessibility: remove the dead Accessible.name/Accessible.description on toggle (or stop ignoring it), and expose Accessible.role / Accessible.checkable / Accessible.checked on root when toggle.visible is true so screen readers announce it as a switch.

reviews.text: Does exactly what the wish (and Nate's comment) asks: a BrightnessItem with range 0..1 shows a Switch instead of a one-step slider, wired the same way as DarkModeItem (NoFocus switch, Space/press action on the delegate, checked bound to the value so outside changes follow). Screenshots show the switch in place of the slider with the existing Off/On status kept, and the rig notes cover 3-level backlights and D-Bus changes. The hidden slider is skipped by Keys.forwardTo, so arrow keys do nothing harmful. Minor nit: the switch has no text unlike the Night Light/Dark Mode switches, which is a deliberate no-new-strings choice and fine.
